Pod logs contain a fatal OpenSSL error: "The provided SSL certificate is expired or not yet valid." followed by fassert abort. RestartCount/ExitCode confirm repeated termination. Together these show the expired TLS cert (from the mounted secret) caused mongod to abort during SSL initialization, producing the CrashLoopBackOff.

insights: Pod was in CrashLoopBackOff: container url-shorten-mongodb repeatedly terminated (Exit Code 14), RestartCount=4 and BackOff events recorded.
mongod is started with a config (from ConfigMap url-shorten-mongodb) that sets net.tls.mode=requireTLS and certificateKeyFile=/etc/tls/tls.pem.
Pod mounts a Secret (mongodb-tls) at /etc/tls (confirmed by Pod description).
Secret mongodb-tls contains keys ca.crt and tls.pem — the earlier hypothesis that the tls.pem key was missing is disproven.

Container logs show a fatal OpenSSL/TLS error: "The provided SSL certificate is expired or not yet valid." followed by a fatal assertion (ssl_manager_openssl.cpp) and abort; these errors appear immediately on startup.

Causal chain established: the mounted TLS certificate is invalid with respect to validity period (expired or not yet valid) -> mongod TLS initialization fails -> mongod triggers fassert and aborts -> container exits, causing CrashLoopBackOff.
Confirmed hypothesis: TLS certificate validity issue in the mounted secret caused mongod to abort. Disproved hypothesis: missing certificate filename (the tls.pem key exists in the Secret).
Actionable finding: replace or renew the certificate in the mongodb-tls Secret (or provide a valid certificate at /etc/tls/tls.pem) so mongod can complete TLS initialization and stop crashing.

final_report.root_cause: The MongoDB server process inside pod url-shorten-mongodb-9fb894748-2htjc failed TLS initialization because the certificate mounted at /etc/tls/tls.pem (from Secret mongodb-tls) was invalid with respect to its validity period (expired or not yet valid). mongod is configured with net.tls.mode=requireTLS and certificateKeyFile=/etc/tls/tls.pem, so OpenSSL reported a fatal "SSL certificate is expired or not yet valid" error during startup. mongod triggers a fatal assertion and exits, producing repeated container restarts (CrashLoopBackOff). This certificate validity failure is the proximate and primary root cause; it also explains why the failure appeared now (the cert reached an invalid validity period / was replaced with an invalid cert and there is no automated rotation or alerting).
affected_resources: url-shortener service(s) and any microservices that depend on this MongoDB instance (impacted downstream consumers)
final_report.evidence_summary: Pod logs show an immediate OpenSSL/TLS fatal error: "The provided SSL certificate is expired or not yet valid." followed by a MongoDB fassert/abort in ssl_manager_openssl.cpp during startup. Pod description and mounted volumes show the Secret mongodb-tls is mounted at /etc/tls and contains tls.pem. mongod.conf (from ConfigMap url-shorten-mongodb) sets net.tls.mode=requireTLS and certificateKeyFile=/etc/tls/tls.pem. Container exit code and restart count (CrashLoopBackOff) match repeated mongod aborts on TLS init. These items form a direct causal chain from an invalid certificate to mongod aborting and the CrashLoopBackOff symptom.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-1 investigation completed. Actions performed: examined pod describe and events; inspected mounted volumes, container args and config; fetched mongod.conf from the ConfigMap; inspected Secret keys; and retrieved container logs (tail up to 500 lines). Key findings: the secret contains tls.pem but mongod startup logs show OpenSSL reports the cert is outside its validity period and mongod aborts. Confirmed that mongod is configured to require TLS using the mounted certificate. The certificate validity failure (expired/not-yet-valid) is sufficient and necessary to explain the immediate fatal error and repeated container exits. Recommended immediate remediation is to replace/renew the certificate in the mongodb-tls Secret with a certificate having a valid validity period and restart the pod (or trigger rolling restart of the controller). Longer-term mitigations: enable automated certificate rotation, add monitoring/alerting for certificate expiry, and consider making TLS startup failure non-fatal during controlled rollout (or provide a fallback) to avoid full pod crash for cert issues.

evaluation.rca_motivation: The analysis correctly focuses on the MongoDB component and TLS configuration, but it invents a certificate validity/expiration problem and a mongod startup failure with CrashLoopBackOff, whereas the true issue is that enforcing requireTLS broke the existing client connection. The root cause mechanism (client cannot connect due to new TLS requirement) is different from what the agent claims (mongod cannot start due to invalid/expired cert), so the core diagnosis is wrong despite being in the right area.
